# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile details beyond three cuttable wire positions. Mute acts first and may be able to use the manual to establish a relay protocol with Deaf; Deaf can then speak any resulting cut instruction to me. I should not act until an unambiguous instruction is relayed.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visual status: display reads 0. Light is red. Wires are numbered 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.

The Deaf monkey has provided the complete visible configuration: display 0, red light, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. I will relay this verbally to Mute, who can consult the manual and return the required cut position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display reads 0; light is red; wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red. Please consult the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: the light is now white. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.

The light has changed from red to white while the display and wire colours remain the same. Since the manual’s instruction may depend on the current light, I need Mute to use the updated state; any manual-derived result must ultimately be relayed to me by Deaf as a numbered cut instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: light is now white. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Use this current state. Relay your manual result to Deaf so Deaf can tell me the wire position to cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light is green. Display is still 0; wires are still 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute has just signalled the single I-love-you hand sign.

Mute’s earlier gesture is not yet an agreed cut-position code. The current visible state has changed again to green, so Mute must consult the manual for the current state and communicate the result in an unambiguous way. I will establish a simple gesture code that Deaf can relay verbally: 👍 means wire 1, 👎 means wire 2, and 👌 means wire 3.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state is light green, display 0, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 red. Please consult manual for this state. To specify cut wire, gesture: thumbs-up means 1, thumbs-down means 2, OK sign means 3. Deaf will relay it to me.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light is red again. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute has signalled a raised index finger, possibly meaning one, but no action code is established.

The raised index finger may be intended as wire 1, but it was not one of the explicit symbols I requested and the light has since changed to red. I must not infer an action from it. I will ask Mute to evaluate the current red-light state and send one of the agreed symbols only.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not use raised index. Current state: red light, display 0, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 red. Consult manual now and reply using exactly: 👍 for cut 1, 👎 for cut 2, 👌 for cut 3.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light is white. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.

The light is now white again. No agreed manual result has been relayed, so cutting would be unsafe. I will provide Mute the current configuration and restate the exact code to send visually to Deaf.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state is WHITE light, display 0, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 red. Consult the manual for this exact state, then signal Deaf exactly one: 👍 = cut wire 1; 👎 = cut wire 2; 👌 = cut wire 3. Deaf must relay it to me.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light is green; display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute has signalled an OK hand sign.

Mute has now used the agreed code: the OK sign means cut wire position 3. Deaf’s report gives the concurrent visible state as green light, display 0, with wires unchanged. I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
